_comment: Content of lab-pws3.psafe3, fed to tests/oracle/pws3_oracle `write`.
Every value is a deliberate throwaway; there is no real credential here.
Field type numbers are formatV3.txt section 3.2 (header) and 3.3 (records).
This file mirrors kdbx-content.xml so a test can compare the two formats
entry for entry: same sentinel, same nesting, same non-ASCII, same shapes.

header.text: Throwaway test safe. Contains no real credential.

header._: 0x04 Timestamp of last save, a 32-bit LE time_t (section 3.1.3)
0x11 Empty group. Section 3.2[16] says this header field MAY repeat, which is the only one that may — the two entries below exist to prove a reader keeps both instead of collapsing them.

records._: The sentinel record. Mirrors Lab/Nested/Router in kdbx-content.xml.

fields._: 0x02 Group: dots are the hierarchy separator (section 3.3[2])
0x06 Password — THE SENTINEL, unique across this repository
0x05 Notes, deliberately longer than the 11 bytes that fit in a field's first block, so the multi-block path is exercised
fields.text: Throwaway fixture entry. The password is a sentinel, not a credential. This note runs well past the eleven bytes that fit in the first block of a field so that the continuation blocks described in formatV3.txt section 3 are exercised.

fields._: 0x0a Password expiry time, in the past on purpose

records._: Non-ASCII everywhere. Mirrors the Ünïcødé entry in kdbx-content.xml.

fields.text: Mixed scripts, a combining mark (é), an astral emoji, and a right-to-left run: ‏عربى‏.

records._: Carries an application-unique field type from the 0xc0-0xdf range (section 4.2.1) and a defined-but-not-implemented one (0x1b Two-Factor Key). Section 4.1 says a reader MUST NOT discard an unknown field — it must preserve it on save. This record is how that gets tested.

fields._: 0x1b Two-Factor Key, binary, listed as not implemented upstream
0xc0 application-unique, must survive a round trip untouched

records._: Zero-length fields are legal (section 2.9.2): absent or zero-length both mean 'use the default'.
